recipes.title: Jachnun
recipes.description: Paper-thin rolled dough baked overnight in a low oven, emerging brown, sweet and yielding.
instructions: Knead flour, sugar, salt and soda with the water into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 10 balls, coat each in samneh, cover and rest another 30 minutes.
Stretch each ball on an oiled surface until thin enough to see through — this is the whole craft. Spread with samneh and roll up.
Pack the rolls tightly into a heavy pot, cover with foil and a lid.
Bake at 100°C overnight, 10–12 hours, until deep brown and tender.
Serve with hard-boiled egg, grated tomato and zhug. The samneh makes this dairy — for a parve jachnun beside soup, use oil or margarine instead.

recipes.title: Kubaneh
recipes.description: A rich yeast bread baked overnight in a sealed pot and torn by hand at dawn — crisp outside, stranded within.
instructions: Froth the yeast with sugar and warm water until foaming, about 10 minutes.
Add flour and salt and knead 8 minutes to a soft, elastic dough. Rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 6 balls, coat generously in samneh and rise another 40 minutes.
Stretch each ball into a sheet, spread with samneh, fold into a square and pack into an oiled pot.
Cover with foil and a lid and bake at 100°C for 9–10 hours.
Serve hot and tear by hand, with grated tomato, zhug and a browned egg.

recipes.title: Malawach
recipes.description: Buttered dough folded again and again, then pan-fried until it peels apart into leaves.
instructions: Knead flour, salt, sugar and water into a soft dough. Rest covered 30 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and coat in samneh. Rest 1 hour.
Stretch each ball very thin, spread with samneh and fold into a square in three folds.
Chill the squares at least 30 minutes — cold dough separates into better layers.
Fry in a dry pan over medium heat, 4–5 minutes a side, until golden and visibly layered.
Serve with grated tomato, zhug and a hard-boiled egg.

recipes.title: Lachuch
recipes.description: A spongy, one-sided flatbread from a fermented batter, its whole surface open with holes.
instructions: Whisk everything into a loose batter the consistency of light cream, with no lumps.
Cover and ferment at room temperature 1–2 hours until bubbling and faintly sour.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with no oil at all.
Pour a ladleful, swirl once, and cook on ONE side only for 2–3 minutes until the surface is covered in holes and the edges lift.
Lift out while the top is still moist and glossy. Never flip it.
Stack and serve with zhug, hilbeh or soup.

recipes.title: Sabaya
recipes.description: Layers of tissue-thin dough soaked in samneh and honey, baked round and cut like a cake.
instructions: Knead flour, salt and water into a soft dough and rest, covered, 40 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and stretch each as thin as it will go.
Lay one sheet in an oiled round tin, brush with samneh and a little honey, and add the next. Repeat through all eight.
Pour the remaining samneh and honey over the top and scatter with sesame.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until deeply golden.
Cool 10 minutes and cut into wedges. Serve with coffee.

recipes.title: Fatut
recipes.description: Torn lachuch fried with eggs and onion — what Yemen does with yesterday's bread.
instructions: Tear the lachuch by hand into bite-sized pieces. Do not cut it — torn edges soak up more.
Fry the onion in the oil over medium heat, 6–7 minutes, until golden.
Add the torn bread and toss for a minute until it takes up the oil.
Beat the eggs with hawaij, salt and pepper and pour in.
Stir 3–4 minutes until the eggs set but stay soft.
Serve at once with green zhug alongside.

recipes.title: Shafut
recipes.description: Lachuch soaked in herbed yogurt — the cold dish that opens a meal on a hot day.
instructions: Blend coriander, dill, garlic, chilli and salt into a smooth green paste.
Stir the paste through the yogurt until it is evenly pale green.
Chill at least 30 minutes — this dish must be cold.
Lay the lachuch in a deep dish and pour the yogurt over until covered.
Let the bread soak for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve cold. This is a dairy dish and is not served beside meat.

recipes.title: Zalabiya
recipes.description: Fried dough coils plunged straight from the oil into cold syrup — crisp outside, sweet all through.
instructions: Whisk flour, yeast and water into a loose batter and ferment 1 hour until bubbling.
Simmer sugar, water and lemon juice 10 minutes into a syrup. Cool completely — hot dough meeting cold syrup is what makes the crust.
Heat deep oil to 175°C.
Pipe the batter through a bag with a small hole in spirals into the oil.
Fry 2–3 minutes until golden, lift out and drop straight into the cold syrup for 30 seconds.
Drain on a rack and serve the same day.

recipes.title: Bint Al-Sahn
recipes.description: "Daughter of the plate" — ten buttered leaves baked together and flooded with hot honey straight from the oven.
instructions: Knead flour, eggs, yeast, salt and a little warm water into a very soft dough. Rise 1 hour.
Divide into 10 small balls and coat each in samneh. Rest 20 minutes.
Stretch one ball until nearly transparent, lay it in a round tin and brush with samneh.
Layer sheet on sheet with samneh between each, through all ten. Scatter nigella on top.
Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until deeply golden.
Heat the honey and pour it over the cake boiling hot the moment it leaves the oven — that is how it runs between the layers instead of sitting on top.

recipes.title: Hawaij Bread
recipes.description: An everyday loaf with olive oil and hawaij, baked hot and torn beside the soup.
instructions: Froth the yeast in warm water for 10 minutes.
Add flour, olive oil, hawaij and salt and knead 8 minutes to a smooth dough.
Rise, covered, 1 hour until doubled.
Shape two flat loaves, set on a tray and scatter with nigella. Rise another 20 minutes.
Bake at 220°C for 22–25 minutes until the base sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool 10 minutes and tear by hand beside soup or zhug.

recipes.title: Yemenite Soup
recipes.description: The soup everything else answers to — meat on the bone, yellow hawaij, and a long low flame.
instructions: Rinse the meat, cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Skim the foam thoroughly — this decides whether the broth runs clear.
Add halved onion, garlic, halved tomatoes and hawaij. Drop to the lowest simmer.
Cook 2 hours with the lid half off, stirring as little as possible.
Add quartered potatoes and cook another 30 minutes.
Correct the salt only at the end — the broth concentrates as it goes.
Scatter chopped coriander and serve with hilbeh, zhug and lachuch.

recipes.title: Trotter Soup
recipes.description: Beef trotters simmered five hours until the broth thickens on its own and sets cold.
instructions: Soak the trotters in cold water for an hour, then scrub and clean them well.
Cover with water, boil 10 minutes and discard that water entirely. Refill with fresh — this step cannot be skipped.
Add onion, garlic, the soaked chickpeas, hawaij and turmeric.
Simmer at the lowest heat 4–5 hours until the meat falls from the bone.
Correct salt and pepper and skim any collected foam.
Serve boiling hot with lachuch. What is left sets in the fridge — the sign it worked.

recipes.title: Saltah
recipes.description: A beef stew served in a stone pot still bubbling, crowned with a white cap of hilbeh.
instructions: Sear the beef in hot oil over high heat until closed on all sides.
Add the onion and fry 8 minutes until golden, then the grated tomato and hawaij.
Add water to cover and simmer, covered, 1 hour over low heat.
Add the potato and cook 20 minutes more until the sauce thickens.
Transfer to a stone or clay pot and return to a fierce boil on the hob.
Crown with hilbeh and zhug while it is still bubbling and bring it to the table in the pot, with lachuch.

recipes.title: Lentil Soup with Hawaij
recipes.description: Red lentils cooked until they collapse entirely into a smooth, sun-coloured broth.
instructions: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear.
Fry onion, carrot and garlic in the olive oil for 8 minutes until the onion turns translucent.
Add the hawaij and stir for 30 seconds — the spice has to meet hot oil to open up.
Add lentils and water and simmer 35–40 minutes until the lentils have fully collapsed.
Blend to the smoothness you like and correct the salt.
Finish with lemon juice and serve with hawaij bread.

recipes.title: Yemenite Ful
recipes.description: Fava beans coarsely crushed with olive oil, garlic and lemon, served hot in a clay bowl.
instructions: Warm the beans with a little of their cooking liquid in a shallow pot.
Crush about a third with a fork and leave the rest whole — the mixed texture is the point.
Add garlic, cumin and salt and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the olive oil and lemon juice and stir off the heat.
Turn into a clay bowl and scatter with chopped tomato.
Spoon zhug over and serve with warm lachuch.

recipes.title: Hareesa
recipes.description: Wheat and meat cooked together for hours until they melt into one thick, savoury mass.
instructions: Soak the wheat overnight in cold water and drain.
Sear the meat in oil, add the onion and fry until golden.
Add wheat, hawaij, cinnamon and water and bring to the boil.
Cook 3–4 hours at the lowest heat, stirring every half hour so it does not catch.
Crush against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon until wheat and meat come together as one thick mass.
Correct the salt, pour hot oil over and serve in deep bowls.

recipes.title: Yemenite Pumpkin Soup
recipes.description: Sweet pumpkin balanced by hawaij and lemon, blended completely smooth.
instructions: Fry onion and carrot in the olive oil 7 minutes until the onion colours.
Add the hawaij and stir half a minute until the aroma rises.
Add pumpkin and water and cook 30 minutes until the pumpkin yields to a spoon.
Blend completely smooth.
Correct the salt and add the lemon juice — it is what keeps the soup from turning sweet.
Serve with a spoonful of zhug in the middle of the bowl.

recipes.title: Beef and White Bean Soup
recipes.description: Beans softened for three hours beside the meat until the broth turns velvety on its own.
instructions: Soak the beans overnight, rinse and drain.
Boil the meat in water and skim until the liquid runs clear.
Add onion, garlic, tomato and hawaij and cook 1½ hours.
Add the beans and cook another 1½ hours at the lowest heat.
Salt only at the end — early salt keeps beans hard.
Scatter coriander and serve with hilbeh and lachuch.

recipes.title: Chicken Soup with Hilbeh
recipes.description: A clear hawaij chicken broth that meets its cap of hilbeh in the bowl, never in the pot.
instructions: Cover the chicken with cold water, bring to the boil and skim carefully.
Add onion, garlic and hawaij and simmer 45 minutes over low heat.
Add carrots and potatoes and cook another 25–30 minutes.
Correct the salt and lift off the fat that has risen.
Ladle into bowls and only then float a spoon of hilbeh on top — in the pot it would break up.
Scatter coriander and serve with lachuch.

recipes.title: Chickpea and Cumin Soup
recipes.description: Chickpeas simmered two hours with cumin and lemon, half blended and half left whole.
instructions: Soak the chickpeas overnight and drain.
Fry onion and garlic in the olive oil 8 minutes, add cumin and hawaij and stir half a minute.
Add chickpeas and water and cook 2 hours until a chickpea crushes between two fingers.
Set a cupful of whole chickpeas aside and blend the rest smooth.
Return the whole ones to the pot and correct the salt.
Finish with lemon juice and a thread of olive oil, and serve with hawaij bread.

recipes.title: Hawaij Roast Chicken
recipes.description: A whole bird rubbed with hawaij, garlic and lemon and roasted until the skin golds and the meat lets go.
instructions: Mix hawaij, garlic, lemon, oil and salt into a thick marinade.
Rub the bird inside and out, and under the breast skin — that is where the marinade actually works.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Lay sliced onion across a roasting tin and set the chicken on it.
Roast covered at 190°C for 60 minutes, then uncovered another 25–30.
Rest 10 minutes before carving and serve with rice and zhug.

recipes.title: Slow-Roast Lamb Shoulder
recipes.description: A whole shoulder given four low hours until it carves with a spoon.
instructions: Score the fat cap in a criss-cross with a sharp knife, without cutting into the meat.
Rub hard with hawaij, cumin, crushed garlic, oil and salt. Chill 2 hours.
Spread roughly cut onion across a deep tin and set the shoulder on it.
Pour hot water into the base of the tin only — never over the meat — and seal tightly with foil.
Roast at 150°C for 3½ hours.
Uncover, raise to 210°C for a final 25 minutes until the surface browns. Serve with the rice that took up the juices.

recipes.title: Yemenite Meatballs in Sauce
recipes.description: Meatballs worked through with coriander and hawaij, simmered in tomato until they drink it in.
instructions: Mix beef, grated onion, coriander, hawaij, crumbs and egg and knead by hand for 2 minutes.
Chill the mixture 20 minutes — a cold meatball holds its shape.
Roll walnut-sized balls and brown them in hot oil on all sides.
Lift the meatballs out and cook the grated tomato in the same oil for 10 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the sauce, cover and simmer 25 minutes over low heat.
Serve with white rice and red zhug.

recipes.title: Chicken Livers with Hawaij
recipes.description: Livers seared fast over high heat with deeply caramelised onion and lemon.
instructions: Dry the livers thoroughly on paper — a wet liver steams instead of searing.
Caramelise the onion in the oil over medium heat for 15 minutes until deeply brown. Set aside.
Raise to very high heat and sear the livers 2 minutes a side, no longer.
Scatter hawaij, salt and pepper and toss for 30 seconds.
Return the onion, add lemon juice and stir off the heat.
Serve immediately — livers left waiting turn grainy.

recipes.title: Beef with Fenugreek
recipes.description: Beef in a thick stew that takes its fenugreek edge only at the very end.
instructions: Soak the ground fenugreek in cold water for 2 hours and drain — soaking draws out the bitterness and leaves the aroma.
Sear the beef in hot oil over high heat in small batches, never all at once.
Add onion and garlic and fry 8 minutes, then the tomato and hawaij.
Add water to partly cover and simmer, covered, 2 hours over low heat.
Stir in the soaked fenugreek for the last 15 minutes only — long cooking turns it bitter.
Scatter coriander and serve with rice or lachuch.

recipes.title: Shabbat Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.description: Chicken and potatoes given three hours together, the potatoes taking everything the bird gives up.
instructions: Mix hawaij, paprika, crushed garlic, oil and salt into a thick paste.
Toss the chicken and the potatoes in it separately, so both are seasoned.
Line a tin with onion, then the potatoes, then the chicken on top — so the fat drips downward.
Pour hot water into the base and seal with foil.
Bake at 160°C for 2½ hours.
Uncover and raise to 220°C for 20 minutes until the skin crisps. Serve with zhug.

recipes.title: Beef Tongue in Hawaij Sauce
recipes.description: Tongue given three hours, peeled hot and sliced thin into a tomato sauce.
instructions: Soak the tongue in cold water for an hour and scrub well.
Simmer in water with a whole onion and bay 2½–3 hours until a fork meets no resistance.
Lift out and peel while it is still very hot — once it cools the skin grips and will not come away.
Fry the garlic in oil, add grated tomato and hawaij and cook 12 minutes.
Slice the tongue thin and lay it in the sauce. Cook together 15 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Lamb in Tomato Sauce
recipes.description: Lamb ribs in a long tomato braise with a whole head of garlic that melts into the sauce.
instructions: Sear the ribs in hot olive oil 3 minutes a side and set aside.
Fry the onion in the same oil 8 minutes, add hawaij and stir half a minute.
Add grated tomato and the whole chilli and cook 10 minutes.
Return the lamb, add the head of garlic halved across, and water to partly cover.
Simmer covered 2 hours over low heat, until the garlic melts and the sauce shines.
Scatter coriander and serve with lachuch for mopping.

recipes.title: Braised Beef Shoulder with Hawaij
recipes.description: A whole shoulder braised slowly in onion and served sliced against the grain.
instructions: Dry the joint and sear it in a heavy pot until deeply brown all over — ten patient minutes.
Lift the meat out and fry the onion in the same fat for 12 minutes until golden.
Return the joint to sit in the onion and scatter with hawaij, garlic, allspice and salt.
Add hot water to a third of the joint's height, cover and cook 3 hours at the lowest heat.
Turn the joint once, halfway through.
Rest 20 minutes before slicing — a hot joint shreds. Slice against the grain and return to the sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken with Cumin and Lemon
recipes.description: Chicken legs in a fast pan braise with freshly toasted cumin and a late squeeze of lemon.
instructions: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan for 90 seconds until fragrant, then grind in a mortar.
Sear the drumsticks in olive oil over high heat until golden all over.
Add onion and garlic and fry 8 minutes.
Scatter in the ground cumin and pepper, add the water and cover.
Cook 35 minutes over low heat until the meat leaves the bone.
Uncover, add the lemon juice and reduce 5 minutes. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Green Zhug
recipes.description: The sauce on every Yemenite table — coriander, hot chilli and garlic, never cooked.
instructions: Wash the coriander and dry it completely — water left on the leaves turns zhug slimy within two days.
Strip only the thick stems; the thin ones carry flavour.
Toast the cumin in a dry pan for 60 seconds and grind.
Pulse coriander, chillies, garlic, cumin, cardamom and salt to a coarse texture — not a purée.
Add the olive oil in a thin stream with a few more short pulses.
Jar it, cover with a film of olive oil and keep refrigerated up to two weeks.

recipes.title: Red Zhug
recipes.description: The deeper, smokier version, built on dried red chillies that are soaked first.
instructions: Soak the dried chillies in hot water 30 minutes until fully soft.
Drain and strip the stems and seeds — seeds add heat but also bitterness.
Toast coriander and caraway seeds in a dry pan for 60 seconds and grind in a mortar.
Blend chillies, garlic, spices and salt into a thick paste.
Work in the olive oil until the paste is glossy and even.
Keep in a jar under a film of oil. It deepens after two days.

recipes.title: Hilbeh
recipes.description: Fenugreek soaked overnight and whipped to a white, airy foam — the crown on every Yemenite soup.
instructions: Soak the ground fenugreek in a cup of cold water overnight. It will swell to double and float.
Pour off the top water carefully — it carries the bitterness — and add fresh cold water.
Repeat the change twice more, an hour apart.
Whip the fenugreek with a fork or mixer for 5–8 minutes until white, light and doubled in volume.
Blend coriander, garlic, chilli, lemon and salt, and fold in gently.
Serve at once on hot soup. Refrigerated, it sets and loses its air.

recipes.title: Hawaij for Soup
recipes.description: The yellow blend this whole kitchen rests on — toasted and ground fresh.
instructions: Toast cumin, coriander, peppercorns, cardamom and cloves in a dry pan over medium heat.
Shake constantly for 3–4 minutes until fragrant and lightly darkened. No further — burnt spice is bitter for good.
Cool completely on a cold plate before grinding.
Grind to a fine powder in a spice mill.
Stir in the ground turmeric — it is not toasted, only blended.
Keep in a sealed jar in the dark for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Hawaij for Coffee
recipes.description: A completely different blend under the same name — cardamom, ginger and cinnamon, for coffee and baking.
instructions: Crack the cardamom pods and take only the black seeds — the husk adds wood, not aroma.
Toast the cardamom seeds and cloves in a dry pan for 2 minutes only.
Cool and grind to a fine powder.
Mix with the ginger, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Keep in a small sealed jar — a small quantity stays fresher.
One teaspoon to a pot of coffee, or a tablespoon into bint al-sahn dough.

recipes.title: Samneh
recipes.description: Clarified butter cooked until the milk solids brown and give it a nutty smell.
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over very low heat, without stirring.
Skim off and discard the white foam that rises in the first ten minutes.
Keep cooking 30–40 minutes. The milk solids will sink and begin to brown.
When the liquid turns fully clear and the solids at the bottom are golden-brown, that is the moment. A second too far and it all turns bitter.
Add fenugreek, turmeric and fennel, stir 30 seconds and take off the heat. The fennel is optional — some households leave it out.
Strain through fine cloth into a jar. This is a dairy product — any jachnun or kubaneh made with it is dairy.

recipes.title: Yemenite Preserved Lemons
recipes.description: Lemons cured in salt and hawaij for three weeks until the peel turns soft and translucent.
instructions: Scrub the lemons well and cut each into quarters without cutting all the way through.
Pack coarse salt generously into every cut.
Press the lemons into a sterilised jar layer by layer, scattering hawaij and chilli between layers.
Press down firmly until the juice rises. Top up with lemon juice until every lemon is fully covered.
Seal and leave at room temperature 3–5 days, turning the jar daily.
Move to the fridge for 3 weeks. Ready when the peel is soft and cuts easily.

recipes.title: Hot Tomato Relish
recipes.description: Tomatoes reduced with chilli and hawaij into a thick, dark spread.
instructions: Score an X in each tomato, blanch 40 seconds and drop into iced water. The skins slip off.
Chop roughly and drain off some of the liquid — less water, less reducing.
Fry the garlic and chopped chilli in the olive oil for 3 minutes only.
Add tomatoes, hawaij, sugar and salt and bring to the boil.
Reduce over medium-low heat for 35 minutes uncovered, until dark and thick.
Keep in a jar in the fridge up to 3 weeks.

recipes.title: Grated Tomato for Jachnun
recipes.description: Jachnun's standing companion — coarsely grated tomato, garlic, lemon and oil, and nothing else.
instructions: Halve the tomatoes and grate them on the coarse side with the skin against your palm — the skin stays in your hand and the flesh falls into the bowl.
Drain a little liquid if the tomatoes are especially watery.
Add crushed garlic, cumin and salt and stir.
Pour in the olive oil and lemon juice and stir again.
Rest 10 minutes before serving so the flavours meet.
Serve cold beside jachnun, kubaneh or malawach, always with zhug alongside.

recipes.title: Garlic and Lemon Sauce
recipes.description: A sharp emulsion of crushed garlic and lemon, served beside meat to cut it.
instructions: Pound the garlic with the coarse salt in a mortar to a completely smooth paste — the salt does the work.
Add the lemon juice in thirds, mixing well after each.
Pour in the olive oil in a very thin stream while stirring constantly, as for mayonnaise.
If it splits, start again with a spoonful of garlic paste and add the split sauce back slowly.
Fold in the chopped coriander.
Serve fresh alongside chicken, lamb or roast potatoes.

recipes.title: Yemenite Coffee
recipes.description: Coffee with hawaij brought to the edge of boiling three times and never once allowed to boil.
instructions: Boil the water with the whole cardamom and sugar in a finjan.
Take it off the heat, add coffee and hawaij and stir once only.
Return to low heat until the foam climbs to the rim — and lift it off at once.
Repeat the rise and lift three times. Coffee that actually boils loses its aroma and turns bitter.
Let it settle for a minute so the grounds sink.
Pour slowly into small cups without shaking the pot.

recipes.title: Qishr
recipes.description: A drink from coffee cherry husks — not coffee, but something between tea and fruit tisane, with ginger.
instructions: Rinse the husks in cold water and drain.
Boil the water with the cinnamon and grated ginger for 5 minutes.
Add the husks and lower the heat.
Simmer 10 minutes until the liquid turns amber — never as dark as coffee.
Add cardamom and sugar and stir until dissolved.
Strain and serve hot in small glasses. An evening drink, after the meal.

recipes.title: Hawaij Tea
recipes.description: Strong black tea infused with cardamom, ginger and cinnamon, served very sweet.
instructions: Boil the water with the ginger slices for 4 minutes.
Take off the heat and add the black tea and hawaij.
Cover and steep exactly 4 minutes — longer draws bitter tannins.
Add sugar and stir until fully dissolved.
Strain into small glasses and add a mint sprig to each.
Serve scalding, with jalah or dates alongside.

recipes.title: Jalah
recipes.description: A bowl of nuts, seeds and dried fruit set out for every visitor.
instructions: Roast the almonds and peanuts at 160°C for 8–10 minutes, shaking once.
Cool completely — warm nuts will steam the raisins and make everything stick.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until they pop.
Combine everything with the raisins, chopped dates and roasted chickpeas.
Scatter cinnamon and salt and toss well.
Keep in a sealed jar. Serve with coffee or tea.

recipes.title: Walnut-Stuffed Dates
recipes.description: Medjool dates filled with spiced walnut and rolled in toasted sesame.
instructions: Slit each date lengthwise with a small knife and lift out the stone without opening it fully.
Toast the walnut halves 5 minutes at 160°C and cool.
Toss the walnuts with hawaij and rose water until lightly coated.
Fill each date with a walnut half and press gently closed.
Roll the open side in the toasted sesame.
Arrange in a shallow bowl and serve with coffee.

recipes.title: Candied Pumpkin in Syrup
recipes.description: Pumpkin cubes simmered slowly in sugar syrup until translucent and still holding their shape.
instructions: Cut the pumpkin into even 3 cm cubes so they all cook at the same rate.
Simmer sugar, water, cinnamon and lemon juice for 8 minutes until the syrup begins to thicken.
Lay the pumpkin in a single layer and drop to the lowest heat.
Cook 40 minutes without stirring — stir and the cubes collapse. Only shake the pan.
Add the lemon zest and cook 5 minutes more until the cubes turn translucent.
Cool completely in the syrup and serve cold with chopped walnuts on top.

recipes.title: Yemenite Date Cake
recipes.description: An oil-and-silan cake spiced with coffee hawaij — parve, and served after meat.
instructions: Chop the dates and pour boiling water over them. Rest 15 minutes until fully softened.
Mash the dates with their soaking liquid into a coarse purée.
Whisk eggs, oil and silan until smooth.
Sift flour, baking powder and hawaij and fold in alternately with the date purée.
Pour into a greased loaf tin and bake at 175°C for 40–45 minutes.
Test with a skewer — it should come out moist but clean. Cool in the tin 20 minutes before turning out.

recipes.title: Yemenite Tahini Halva
recipes.description: Raw tahini and sugar syrup worked together and left to set into a crumbling block.
instructions: Mix the raw tahini with the cardamom and warm it slightly — cold tahini will not marry with the syrup.
Cook sugar, water and lemon juice to 118°C on a sugar thermometer. You cannot do this without one — the temperature decides whether the halva crumbles or stays sticky.
Pour the hot syrup into the tahini in a thin stream, stirring fast with a spatula.
Keep stirring 2–3 minutes until the mixture thickens and starts to leave the sides.
Fold in the pistachios and turn into a small paper-lined tin.
Press down firmly, set 4 hours at room temperature and cut into cubes.

recipes.title: Sweet Malawach with Honey
recipes.description: Malawach fried in samneh and served straight away with warm honey and nuts.
instructions: Warm the honey with the cardamom in a small pot over low heat until fully runny. Do not boil it.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes and cool.
Fry each malawach sheet in a tablespoon of samneh, 3 minutes a side, until golden and separating into layers.
Move to a plate and pour the warm honey over at once — on cooled malawach the honey just sits on top.
Scatter with walnuts and cinnamon.
Serve hot. The samneh makes this dairy — not after a meat meal.

recipes.title: Cardamom Rice Pudding
recipes.description: Round rice cooked slowly in milk and cardamom until velvety, served warm with pistachios.
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, but not entirely — some starch is needed for the texture.
Cook the rice in 2 cups of water for 10 minutes until absorbed.
Add the milk gradually, a cup at a time, stirring slowly and continuously.
Cook over low heat 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes so it does not catch.
Add sugar and cardamom for the last 5 minutes — sugar added early stops the rice softening.
Off the heat, stir in the rose water and serve warm with pistachios and cinnamon.
